significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) law plus a causal mechanism: an internal truth readout rises with graded entity familiarity while knowledge and veracity are held fixed, peaks in the "recognized-but-unknown cell," and predicts later hallucination, with an "identifiable component" mediating the leak. This fixes expectations across a family of familiarity/knowledge conditions rather than merely showing that truth is decodable, as in Marks and Tegmark's The Geometry of Truth (COLM 2024); it establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—familiar-entity falsehoods are over-believed—and a mechanistic explanation linking recognition, truth readout, and hallucination. A verified-negative result on the central H2 would distinguishably rule out recognition contamination as the explanation for familiarity-associated hallucination, although failure of one of the auxiliary decoding or localization clauses would be less decisive. Topic-substitution check: replacing the graded, knowledge-controlled predictive coupling with the generic LLM-beliefs topic would not support this score; the specific cross-channel law and causal mediation are materially stronger than the topic's obvious first hypothesis.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the "per-claim recognition-to-truth leak," explicitly proposed as a predictor "read before any query," alongside "retrieval gating when recognition is high but knowledge is low" and "abstention calibrated on leak magnitude." This is ex ante rather than post hoc and gives auditors or deployment practitioners an action window before an associated hallucination, while the steering component supplies an additional intervention handle. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion still predicts a graded peak in recognized-but-unknown cases and a leak–hallucination coupling, so more than a search procedure transfers, although the hypothesis does not assert universal numerical thresholds or reach beyond the class of LLM factual-claim tasks. Topic-substitution check: generic research on LLM beliefs would provide neither this pre-query predictor nor the gating rule, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handles rather than the topic's general importance.
